messages.author: 9ff02ee016b8a9e0
messages.subject: SQL Backend?
parts:
Hi, I'd like to deploy an app with a MySQL backend.  Can that be done on Shinyapps.io?  If not with MySQL, with any other SQL or NoSQL backend?

Scott

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: SQL Backend?
parts:
Scott,

We currently don't support running any other services besides Shiny applications. That said, we've considered adding the ability to deploy additional services such as mysql, but we are not likely to take on this work any time soon.

In the mean time, you can always connect your application to a 3rd party hosting service with the database of your choosing. There are a number of hosting providers for various databases that your application could talk to (provided there are R drivers).

You could take a look at:

Amazon RDS (Oracle/MySQL)
ObjectRocket (MongoDB)
Cloudant (CouchDB)

-Andy

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: SQL Backend?
parts:
Alok,

As you pointed out, using SQLite may be a good option. However, I wanted to bring up a few points which are outlined in the Application Instances section of the Getting Started Guide:

Files that are written to the local file system (such as SQLite database) of a running application are not persisted across deployments or instance restarts. In other words, if you were to re-deploy the application, the files that were written before you re-deployed, would be lost. Additionally, sometimes application instances may need to restarted (to either balance load across our servers, or to recover from a server failure). In this case the files written locally would be also lost.

If you were to use SQLite in a readonly manner, this would not be an issue. 

Additionally, it's worth noting that shiny-server (which ShinyApps uses internally) does create multiple R processes to serve requests to an application. While its possible for multiple processes to open a SQLite database, only one process may write to it.

messages.subject: Re: SQL Backend?
parts:
Hello,
I used SQLite with Shiny. Works well on local machine but when the SQL executes on shiny server it doesn't find the table.
The error: 
Error in sqliteSendQuery(con, statement, bind.data) : 
error in statement: no such table: TblResult

My Code:
#OPEN LIBRARIES
library("shiny")  #SHINY LIBRARY
library("RSQLite")	#SQLITE LIBRARY
library("DBI")

#SET CONNECTION TO EXISTING SQLITE DATABASE 
sqlite <- dbDriver("SQLite")	#LOAD DRIVER
candb <- dbConnect(sqlite, dbname= "WaterQuality_STEP_V8.sqlite")	#LOAD DB

#IMPORT ALL DISTINCT CONSTITUENT NAMES FROM DATABASE
AllCanConst <- data.frame(dbGetQuery(candb, "SELECT DISTINCT TblResult.Constituent_ID FROM TblResult ORDER BY TblResult.Cons tituent_ID")) 

ListAllCanConst <- AllCanConst[,1]	#SELECTS THE FIRST COLUMN ONLY

#DISCONNECT WITH SQLITE DATABASE  
dbDisconnect(candb) 

Can anyone tell me what's wrong with the code?
It is possible to use SQLite database within the shiny web framework right?

Thanks!

messages.author: e54723a703037086
messages.subject: Re: SQL Backend?
parts: I found my mistake. Shiny apps on your local machine is not case sensitive but the shinyapps.io web server is. The case of one the letters in my database file name was different in my code. This resulted in the app not looking through the database and thus giving "no such table" error.
